Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1239 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY REGION...AND PARTS OF THE NORTHEAST...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong to severe storms may occur from Iowa across Wisconsin
and into Upper Michigan Friday, with areas of strong/damaging wind
gusts and isolated marginal hail. Other storms may produce locally
damaging gusts over parts of the Northeast.

...IA...southeast MN...WI...Upper MI...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will move across the northern Plains
and into the Upper MS Valley, with a cold front extending from
northwest WI into IA by late afternoon. A moist air mass with 70s F
dewpoints will exist ahead of the front, contributing to 2000-3000
J/kg MUCAPE. Supporting the potentially strong instability will be
relatively cool 500 mb temperatures to around -10 C.

Storms are likely to form during the afternoon along the front with
scattered marginal hail or strong wind gusts. Deep-layer shear will
not be particularly strong. Some potential may develop for an MCS
over southern areas including IA, and this area will be monitored
for potential greater wind probabilities.

...Northern VA into PA and southern NY...
Midlevel southwesterlies around 25 kt will exist across the
northeastern states on Friday, with weak height falls occurring as a
primary upper trough moves across the Great Lake region. In the low
levels, west/southwest winds around the Atlantic high will maintain
a warm/moist air mass, which when heated during the afternoon should
yield up to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE, especially near the coastal areas
where dewpoints will be higher.

Despite lack of any surface boundaries, model consensus is for
scattered storms to develop from northern VA/MD into central to
eastern PA and across southern NY during the afternoon. Shear will
be weak but a few clusters of storms may produce gusty winds.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0211 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM NEBRASKA
INTO PARTS OF IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI...

...SUMMARY...
A corridor of damaging winds may develop Saturday afternoon and
evening from Nebraska into Iowa/Northern Missouri.

...Mid to Lower MO Valley...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will persist across the northern
Plains into the Great Lakes on Saturday, as the main upper wave
rotates northeast from Ontario into Quebec. The southern periphery
of this stronger flow aloft will remain over the middle to lower MO
Valley, with a warm front developing across NE and IA. Strong
heating will occur east of a surface low either in western NE or KS,
with south winds resulting in a deep mixed layer by afternoon.

Storms are expected to form over NE, and possibly move into IA or MO
through evening in the form of an MCS. This would be fueled by a
strengthening southerly low-level jet as well, suggesting an
organized system may occur. For now, low probabilities have been
added due to uncertainty with placement of any such corridor.
Damaging winds would be the main concern.

...Mid Atlantic...
Scattered afternoon storms will again be likely over much of the
eastern states on Saturday, within a modest southwest flow regime. A
high PW environment will remain in place, supporting an uncapped air
mass and conditional/localized wind risk. Predictability is low at
this time given possible antecedent rain or thunderstorm areas, but
low probabilities for wind could be added in later updates.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 081200Z - 131200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Saturday/D4...
Southwest midlevel winds of only 25 kt will exist across the
Northeast, while low-level moisture remains in place supporting up
to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE with poor lapse rates aloft. This will support
daytime thunderstorms over a large area from the Appalachians into
the Northeast, and a few severe gusts cannot be ruled out.
Otherwise, normal gusty outflow winds are to be expected.

To the west, an area of stronger instability is forecast across the
Mid MO Valley, where northwesterly midlevel winds of 35 kt will
exist along the southern periphery of a trough sweeping across the
Upper Great Lakes. Evening/overnight storms may occur across parts
of eastern NE, IA, and MO, and instability may be large enough to
warrant at least low severe probabilities as the event nears in
time.

...Sunday/D5...
Drying will occur aloft over parts of the Northeast as a wave moves
into Quebec, but substantial low-level moisture will still support
scattered thunderstorms ahead of a cold front across the Mid
Atlantic. Shear will again be weak, but perhaps enough mean wind
speeds will exist for storms to be mobile/produce areas of strong
gusts.

To the west, low-level moisture is forecast to shift a bit farther
north into the Dakotas, and this will occur beneath stronger
northwest flow aloft. This area bears watching in later outlooks, as
wind profiles may somewhat favor supercells. Predictability is
currently low.

...Mon/D6 to Wed/D8...
While predictability decreases further during this time frame,
moderate west to northwest flow aloft will remain from the upper MS
Valley across the Great Lakes, which will spread into the Northeast
D7/D8. If a wave does amplify within this flow regime, a corridor of
damaging winds could develop given upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints
along/south of the mean frontal zone (roughly IA to NY/PA by end of
the period). Model variation is currently too great to depict an
precise corridor.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1246 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
SOUTHEAST KANSAS...NORTHEAST OKLAHOMA...SOUTHWEST MISSOURI AND FAR
NORTHWEST ARKANSAS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible this
afternoon and evening over parts of Great Plains and Ozarks.
Isolated severe gusts will also be possible today from the
Mid-Atlantic northward into New York.

...Northern Oklahoma/Southern Kansas/Southwest Missouri/Far
Northwest Arkansas...
An upper-level trough will move eastward toward the mid Mississippi
Valley today. At the surface, a quasi-stationary front will be
located from far northern Oklahoma east-northeastward into
south-central Missouri, along which dewpoints will be in the 60s and
lower 70s F. As surface temperatures warm during the day, moderate
instability will develop along and near the front, with the RAP
forecasting MLCAPE to increase into the 2000 to 3000 J/kg range.
During the afternoon, low-level convergence will become focused near
the front with scattered thunderstorm development taking place from
southern Kansas into southwest Missouri. These storms will move
southeastward into northern Oklahoma and far northwestern Arkansas
by the early to mid evening. 

In addition to the moderate instability, RAP forecast soundings
early this evening near the front have 0-6 km shear in the 35 to 40
knot range with 0-3 km lapse rates near 8 C/km. This environment
will support a severe threat. A mixed mode is expected with
supercells and multicell line segments both possible. Supercells
will be capable of severe wind gusts and hail, while the stronger
line segments will be associated with primarily a wind-damage
threat. The severe threat could persist into the mid to late
evening.

...Mid-Atlantic/New York/Far Western New England...
Mid-level flow will be southwesterly over the Northeast today. At
the surface, a trough will be located from the Atlantic Coastal
Plains of Virginia north-northeastward into the southeastern New
York. As surface temperatures warm today, thunderstorms will develop
in the foothills of the Appalachians, moving east-northeastward into
the lower elevations and toward the surface trough. Surface
dewpoints near the trough will be in the lower to mid 70s F, which
will contribute to moderate destabilization by early afternoon.
MLCAPE is forecast to peak in the 2000 to 3000 J/kg range, which
combined with steep low-level lapse rates will support an isolated
wind-damage threat.

...Western Nebraska/Southern South Dakota...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place over much of the
north-central U.S. today. At the surface, an axis of low-level
moisture will set up from western Nebraska into far southern South
Dakota, where dewpoints will be in the 60s F. Near this axis, model
forecasts show a pocket of moderate instability this afternoon with
MLCAPE peaking in the 2000 to 3000 J/kg range. Although large-scale
ascent will be weak, any cell that can initiate near the instability
axis could be capable of producing isolated severe gusts.

..Broyles/Supinie.. 08/06/2026

$$
